book_role.title: Introduction to Constitutional Capitalism
book_role.note: The public book remains the readable entry. The website is the living school of thought.

domain_tree.title: Human Flourishing Index
domain_tree.central_promise: Did human life improve? Every proposal should answer whether it measurably increases human flourishing — not GDP alone.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Human Flourishing Measurement

domain_tree.title: Constitutional Family Doctrine
domain_tree.central_promise: Strong families create strong communities. Children are the republic's greatest long-term asset — with inherent dignity — and public institutions strengthen families rather than replace them whenever possible.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Family, Childhood Flourishing, and Intergenerational Prosperity

domain_tree.title: Assistance Doctrine
domain_tree.central_promise: Guarantee security while dismantling dependency. Different pathways for different circumstances. Every additional hour of productive work should leave a household better off. Destination: income, ownership, and full community participation — not warehousing and not abandonment.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Automate the routine. Elevate the human.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Assistance, Security, Participation, and Pathways to Independence

domain_tree.title: Federalism Doctrine
domain_tree.central_promise: A federal government limited, capable, transparent, and focused — not weak. Power remains local unless national coordination, uniformity, or constitutional-rights protection is required.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Strong enough to protect the republic. Restrained enough to respect local self-government.
branches: Return of authority to lower levels
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Federal Role, Subsidiarity, and National Minimum Standards

domain_tree.title: Popular Sovereignty & People’s Branch
domain_tree.central_promise: The people are the continuing sovereign authority — a fourth branch and first source of authority — with structured powers to propose, reject, recall, audit, and amend, bounded by a hard rights floor and an accountable People’s Court.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Independent enough to protect rights. Accountable enough that abuse cannot hide behind independence.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Popular Sovereignty, Direct Democracy, and Judicial Accountability

domain_tree.title: Equal Standing Before the Constitution
domain_tree.central_promise: Every person stands equal before the Constitution — equal protection and equal accountability. Conduct before status whenever constitutionally and practically possible. No one above the law; no one beneath its protection.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: The Constitution should hear the evidence before it sees the person.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Equal Standing, Blind-Stage Justice, and Equal Access

domain_tree.title: Constitutional Citizenship Doctrine
domain_tree.central_promise: Self-government requires education. Graduate every citizen prepared for responsible participation — democracy as a skill learned through experience, not merely a right activated by birthday. Civic service strengthens participation while remaining viewpoint-neutral.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Civic Preparation, Youth Participation, and Constitutional Citizenship

domain_tree.title: Community Safety, Justice, and Restoration
domain_tree.central_promise: Not more incarceration, not less accountability — more safety, more restoration, and far less human potential permanently discarded. Never classify people as unworthy of reentry; when continuing extreme danger requires custody, use public, humane, reviewable secure campuses — not exile or private profit from confinement.

domain_tree.title: Public Service and the 21st-Century State
domain_tree.central_promise: Government should become invisible—but never unaccountable. Continuously reduce administrative friction while improving public service; automate the routine, elevate the human; organize around life events, not agency charts.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Government should become invisible—but never unaccountable.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Government Capacity, Public Service, and Institutional Modernization

domain_tree.title: Citizen-Service Government — Serve Without Sacrifice
domain_tree.central_promise: Public office is constitutional service, not a pathway to a privileged class. Ordinary working people can serve without sacrificing livelihood or family security — then return to productive community life. Serve without sacrifice. Govern without privilege. Return without penalty.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Serve without sacrifice. Govern without privilege. Return without penalty.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Citizen-Service Government, Public Office Equality, and Civic Access

domain_tree.title: Human Capital Doctrine
domain_tree.central_promise: Every child deserves a meaningful pathway to productive adulthood. Build human capital infrastructure — multiple respected pathways of equal dignity — and pilot regional academies that make home stronger.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Human Capital Infrastructure, Pathways, and Regional Academies

domain_tree.title: Education
domain_tree.note: Education content is seeded under Human Capital Doctrine (CC-WEB-HUMANCAPITAL); keep this node for navigation compatibility until branch pages mature.

domain_tree.title: Essential Systems
domain_tree.central_promise: Design essential systems so private innovation and investment are rewarded while the public interest remains protected — evaluate banking, insurance, healthcare, and pharmaceuticals through incentives and outcomes, not inherent-corruption conclusions.
chapter_method: What is this system supposed to accomplish?
Where are the incentives well aligned, and where are they not?
What reforms would better align the system with Constitutional Capitalism?
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Essential Systems: Banking, Insurance, Healthcare, and Preventive Design

domain_tree.title: Health, Human Capacity, and Community Care
domain_tree.central_promise: No Arkansan should be condemned to poorer health because of their ZIP code, income, employment status, or distance from a major hospital. We will fund the capacity to keep communities healthy—not merely the transactions generated after people become sick.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Basic health security follows the person. Supplemental choice may follow the market.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Constitutional Health System, Rural Capacity Financing, and Prevention Dividends

domain_tree.title: Prosperous Aging System
domain_tree.central_promise: No earned Social Security benefit will be taken away. Current retirees and people nearing retirement remain fully protected. Constitutional Capitalism adds ownership, healthcare security, housing stability, transportation, energy affordability, and community dividends so retirement becomes security and participation—not mere survival.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Social Security keeps you from falling. Constitutional Capitalism helps you continue rising.
branches: Local Aging and Family Care Networks
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Shared Prosperity Retirement, Social Security Floor, and Local Aging Networks

domain_tree.title: Community Prosperity Accounts
domain_tree.central_promise: Every American should have the opportunity to own a stake in the long-term prosperity of the community they help build — complementing, not replacing, diversified retirement savings.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: What if citizens could become long-term investors in the prosperity of the communities they help build?
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Community Equity, Community Investment Units, Civic Equity Credits, and Local Capital Formation

domain_tree.title: Community Food Security System
domain_tree.central_promise: Every community should have the capacity to provide a meaningful share of its essential food needs while remaining connected to broader markets that increase resilience and economic opportunity. Food is critical infrastructure — local resilience first, trade as complementary strength, never export-only staples.

domain_tree.title: Local Food and Family Farm Prosperity
domain_tree.central_promise: A farmer who produces healthy food, restores the soil, protects water, employs local people, and feeds the surrounding community should earn a dependable income, build equity, pass the farm forward, and share in the prosperity of the local food economy.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Is the land healthier, are the farmers more prosperous, are the people better fed, and is more of the wealth remaining in the community?
branches: Rural Food and Farm Service Corps
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Family Farm Wealth Engines, Local Markets, Regional Food Utilities, and Regenerative Stewardship

domain_tree.title: Energy Sovereignty and the People’s Energy Dividend
domain_tree.central_promise: Power America first. Strengthen the free world second. Return the profit to the people. Produce reliable affordable energy for households, communities, industry, and defense; export genuine surplus; and ensure durable public and community ownership of the resulting wealth.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Serve the people first. Strengthen the nation second. Export the surplus third.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Energy Sovereignty, Public Energy Returns, and National Energy Prosperity

domain_tree.title: Resource Sovereignty and Community Stewardship
domain_tree.central_promise: Natural resources belong first to the place that bears the extraction, consumption, congestion, pollution, and long-term risk. Private enterprise may profit — the affected community must receive a direct, permanent, measurable return. The greater the consumption, scarcity, risk, or damage, the greater the obligation to the affected community.

domain_tree.title: Democracy, Representation, and Distributed Government
domain_tree.central_promise: Political authority is held in trust, never owned. Power must remain divided, visible, reviewable, locally rooted where possible, and continuously returnable to the people.

domain_tree.title: Constitutional Transparency and the People's Ledger
domain_tree.central_promise: Government holds public information in trust: presumed open unless a constitutionally or legally justified reason protects it — every public dollar and major action leaves a reviewable trail.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Constitutional Transparency, Public Records, and Accountability Systems

domain_tree.title: Civic Wealth — Investment Through Contribution
domain_tree.central_promise: Thank you for strengthening the republic. Now the republic will invest in your next chapter of building it. Every completed chapter of public service expands opportunity for ownership, leadership, and community prosperity — not permanent dependence or political privilege.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Investment through contribution — not benefit stacks.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Civic Wealth Ladder, Civic Investment Accounts, and Constitutional Service Pathways

domain_tree.title: Constitutional Defense and National Resilience
domain_tree.central_promise: Peace through strength under the Constitution — neither hawkish nor pacifist. The Armed Forces defend liberty and deter aggression; military power never replaces constitutional government, diplomacy, or the sovereignty of the people. A nation is strongest when its communities are strong.
domain_tree.iconic_phrase: Victory is measured by wars prevented.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Constitutionally Defensive Military Power, Veterans Civic Pathways, and National Resilience

domain_tree.title: Build Your Community
domain_tree.central_promise: Same principles. Different playbooks. Start from assets and people; attract, keep, and expand ownership; measure progress — Community OS is a design agenda, not an operating product yet.
domain_tree.research_domain_title: Community Operating System, Playbooks, and Implementation Pathways

life_path_tree.title: A Child
life_path_tree.prompt: What does Constitutional Capitalism mean for someone born today?

essential_infrastructure_principle.text: Essential infrastructure that enables participation in modern economic life should be broadly accessible.
essential_infrastructure_principle.note: Principle before institutional model. Public, private, cooperative, or hybrid solutions remain open design questions.
